description: Home Depot is the world’s largest home improvement retailer, operating almost 2,500 superstores in all 50 U.S. states. Home Depot sells items including appliances, tools, and hardware in its stores and online. As of 2026, it employed 472,000 associates, who are known for wearing distinctive orange uniform aprons. To expand beyond stores and e-commerce, Home Depot has invested billions in professional builder and contractor businesses. In 2024, it acquired SRS Distribution, a large distributor of building products. The deal was valued at $18.25 billion and is the largest in the retailer’s history.

title: Home Depot

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription:
Rising inflation, tighter consumer budgets, and slower housing market activity didn’t stop the home improvement retail chain from raking in $157 billion in sales in the 2022 fiscal year, a 4% increase from the previous year.

  • In February 2023, the company announced that it would raise its starting wage to $15 an hour for its workers in the U.S. and Canada, following some of its retail competitors in taking similar steps.

  • Edward “Ted” Decker, who had been named CEO of Home Depot in March 2022, became chairman on Oct. 1, 2022. Decker replaced Craig Menear in both posts.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Despite dealing with supply-chain problems and shortages, Home Depot brought in over $150 billion in sales in the 2021 fiscal year, as the company proved a resource for new and existing homeowners looking to redecorate and renovate. More recently, as lockdown DIY projects have trailed off and inflation has surged, Home Depot’s fortunes have wavered; its stock declined more than 30% in the first six months of 2022. In a bid to enhance its e-commerce experience, the company has partnered with Walmart for delivery services and created a new executive role to oversee and streamline online orders.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Home Depot made a number of moves that could have hampered business in 2020, including eliminating spring sales events and limiting the number of shoppers in stores, at least at the start of the outbreak. But making shoppers and employees comfortable paid off for the home-improvement giant, whose sales rose 20% to hit $132 billion as consumers enhanced their homes with DIY projects during lockdowns. Home Depot is set up well for the next phase: Consumers are starting to gravitate toward investing in the bigger projects executed by contractors and handymen, who are behind 45% of Home Depot’s sales.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: The home improvement leader has continued to best its competitors—including Lowe’s. Credit both the ongoing effort to spruce up store brands and new technology tools that let store workers see a fuller picture of a shopper’s spending history as it offers opportunities for upselling. The company's e-commerce operation grew more than 20% last year. Home Depot has also gingerly expanded its assortment, dipping its toes into home furnishings and decor, to get more spending from each shopper visit. While the housing market could be heading for bumpy times in a recession, Home Depot appears to be gathering the tools it needs to keep outperforming rivals.
